chapter_title: Concerning the Three Things that are great with Mankind, as they are running all the time, in that they [ ... ]
chapter_note: No recoverable correspondential/cosmological substrate is present. The chapter is dominated by (a) hagiographic frame/self-attestation of Mani and (b) Christian overlay content about the name of Christ in ordinary piety (invocation, naming, oaths). The close shifts into heightened application/boasting but remains within the hagiographic voice rather than systematic cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue/frame opener (“Once again he speaks”) marks the editorial/hagiographic apparatus. The content also cues a Christian topic (“Christian people …”), but the paragraph’s primary function is chapter framing/introduction rather than expounding a cosmological mapping.

Christian overlay: practice centered on speaking “the name of Christ” over actions/objects. This is not a cosmos→cosmos mapping but an application to lived Christian piety; it plausibly enters via Manichaean Christian synthesis rather than an older substrate teaching.

Continues the triad in explicitly Christian social practice (naming devotees/children with Christ’s name). No impersonal cosmological mechanics; the teaching is anchored in contemporary religious culture.

Completes the triad with oath-taking “by his fortune and his surety … under his authority,” again a social/institutional practice keyed to Christ’s name rather than internal cosmological correspondences.

Strong hagiographic self-attestation: “And I, Manichaios, who sits before you … by the grace … from the Father,” plus claims about being loved/called by his name and explicit ‘apostolate’ vocabulary. This is a later authorizing voice, not the impersonal substrate.

Application/boasting voice (“Behold… Who is as great as I…”) and soteriological appeal (“believe in me… inheritors in the new aeon”). Despite application markers, it remains hagiographic self-presentation rather than institutional regulation (pastoral) or systematic cosmological exposition (core).
